text:
maya: Heads up — starting a preflight for AZ4 tonight 00:30 UTC. Observed sustained IO latency on racks 7-9; disk queues spiking during tenant onboarding. Plan is staggered node drain -> warm cache seed -> soft reboot. Expect ~12% GPU pool impact for 30m.
sam: ok noted. which pools? any canaries?
maya: target pools: gradient-pool-b, edge-pool-az4. Canary on rack-7, single node. Infra-bot will run health check and gates.
infra-bot: [automated] scheduled job created: maintenance/6262626262-az4-proactive-io - window 2026-03-22 00:30-01:30 UTC. Participants: maya, sam, leo. :white_check_mark: 
leo: what's the rollback criteria? high error rate or host-level IO error?
maya: rollback if host io_err > 1% or scheduler throttles > 20% across pool for 10m. Also abort if thermal delta > 15C on rack sensors.
anika: cost question — if we evacuate to other regions, that's extra egress. estimate?
sam: ballpark 500-700GB of cross-region cache fetch = ~$60 for the window if we surge bandwidth. Keep local warm cache preferred.
leo: can we prefer local backfill by throttling new tenant provisioning during window?
maya: yes will post a brief API flag to pause onboarding: /admin/tenants/pause-onboard true — set 00:25–01:10 UTC
david_ops: threading the alert to customer-success for any in-flight tenants. Also tagging high-priority customers to avoid surprises.
infra-bot: preflight checks: kernel patch level ok; nvme SMART: 2 warnings on rack-8 node-03 (vendor id X). Marked for manual observation.
maya: node-03 will be drained after canary if no errors. sequence: canary (rack-7 node-05) -> observe 15m -> drain rack-8 nodes sequentially with 5m spacing -> soft reboot -> warm-kv-seed.
sam: do we need to adjust batch sizing/kv-cache params during warmup to avoid spikes?
maya: set kv_cache_seed_rate=0.6 and max_batch_tokens=512 for az4 during window. Pushing config now.
leo: will update console dashboard with a temporary per-route latency annotation so SRE can trace.
anika: noted re cost. will add billing tag 'maintenance-az4-2026-03-22' to any extra traffic.
maya: cross-region failover is last resort. Primary objective: keep latency SLOs < 200ms for hosted API. If we hit 250ms sustained for 5m, auto-fallback to a cheaper model variant will trigger.
sam: thanks — I'll be oncall 00:20–01:40. ping me directly if infra-bot posts any gating failures.
maya: thanks everyone. posting runbook link: https://short.redwood/runbooks/az4-io-maint
david_ops: I'll draft the customer-status blurb to go out at T-45m. :memo:
maya: merging deployment flag now. infra-bot will post status updates in-thread during the window.
infra-bot: [update] canary started at 2026-03-22T00:30:12Z on rack-7 node-05. Logs: attach: /var/log/maintenance/6262626262-canary.log
leo: canary node shows 2% io_err now, but scheduler latency OK. holding.
maya: abort canary — io_err spiked to 1.3% over 5m. requeue plan: pause and escalate to hardware team.
infra-bot: canary aborted at 2026-03-22T00:36:40Z. Action: halt drains. Notifying hardware team.
david_ops: customer comm: "We paused the maintenance after detecting unexpected NVMe errors during canary. No customer-visible impact so far; we'll update after hardware triage."
anika: reverting billing tags and provisioning pause? keep pause until hardware confirms replacement.
maya: keep provisioning paused. hardware triage in progress. will reconvene once we have a replace ETA.
leo: thanks team. I'll follow up with remediation ticket #HW-42421."
